sentences.text: This is a claim petition filed by the petitioner claiming compensation of .50,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the injuries sustained by him in the accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 15.03.2024 at about 09.00 to 09.15 a.m., he was traveling on Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-06-HS- 1565, as a pillion rider, from Tumakur side towards Akshaya College side and when he reached in front of MAR Swimming pool, Arakere,
Tumakuru - Koratagere SH-33 Road, Tumakuru District, a Lorry bearing Regn.No.AP-04-TX-9855,
driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to the motor cycle.

Due to the accident, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and thereafter, he was shifted to Sridevi Hospital, Tumakuru and then shifted to Hosmat Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and spent huge amount towards hospitalization, medical expenses,
conveyance, food, nourishment and other incidental expenses.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was studying final year Diploma at Akshaya Polytechnic College, Tumakuru and earning a sum of .30,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of lorry by its driver.
The respondents, being the owner and insurer, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. In pursuance of notice, both the respondents have appeared before the tribunal through their respective counsel and filed their separate written statement.
4. In the Written Statement, the respondents denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.

The respondents also denied age, occupation and income of petitioner as well as place,
time and manner of accident.
Further respondents contended that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.

Further contended that the driver of the lorry has driven the lorry in slow manner, to extreme left side of the road by following traffic rules, at that time the rider of motorcycle namely Kiran, driven the same at high speed in a negligent manner and hit the lorry.
Further contended that at the time of accident the driver of lorry by name Manoj was very experienced in driving and he was having valid and effective driving license to drive the lorry.

The respondent No.1, the owner of the said lorry, insured his lorry with respondent No.2 and at the time of accident, the policy of said lorry is in force and also the said lorry is having road permit to transfer the goods
. The amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of petition.

5. 2nd respondent, in the written statement, contended that the alleged accident is said to have taken place on 15.03.2024 but reported to the police on 16.03.2024 and there was delay in reporting the alleged accident to the police.

Further respondent no 2 admitted the aspect of issue of insurance policy vide No.61120731230100000035 valid from 29.04.2023 to 28.04.2024, in respect of lorry belonging to 1st respondent and contended that the liability, if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.

Further the alleged accident was due to negligence of the rider of motor cycle who was unmindful of traffic and movement of vehicles on road without following lane discipline Manish R vs Maheshwar Reddy Y on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64515664/
2 and giving way to the oncoming vehicles, suddenly moved to the middle of the road and dashed to the lorry.

sentences.text: Further contended that the rider of motor cycle had no valid and effective driving license to ride the motor cycle and was not wearing safety helmet while proceeding on motor cycle.
Further the driver of insured lorry also had no valid driving license authorizing him to drive the lorry at the time of alleged accident.
The amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of petition.

6. On the basis of above pleadings, this tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 15.03.2024 at about 09.00 to 09.15 a.m., infront of MAR swimming pool, Arakere, Tumkur, Koratagere SH-33 Road, Tumakur District, when petitioner was proceeding on a Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-06-HS-1565 as a pillion rider,
due to the rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Regn.No.AP-04- TX-9855 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition? If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3. What order or award?

7. In order to prove the contention of the petition, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and examined Dr.Nagaraj.B.N., working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Center,
Bengaluru as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16 and closed evidence of his side.

9.

Findings of this tribunal on the above issues are under:-
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative;
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative; Issue No.3: As per final order for the following:-

10. Issue No.1:- The petitioner contended that on 15.03.2024 at about 09.00 to 09.15 a.m., accident occurred in front of MAR Swimming pool, Arakere, Tumkur, Koratagere SH-33 Road, Tumakur District, when petitioner was proceeding on Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-06-HS-1565, as a pillion rider, due to the rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Regn.No.AP-04-TX-9855 by its driver in which he sustained grievous injuries.

sentences.text: Further, in order to prove accident, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.2, first information statement.

On perusal of Ex.P.2, first information statement, friend of petitioner by name Shivakumar S/o Narasappa has lodged complaint with police on 16.03.2024 pertaining to the accident occurred on 15.03.2024.
The police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337 & 304(A) of IPC and U/s.134(A&B), 187 of M.V.Act.
In the first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle.
The accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
Ex. P.1
discloses the aspect of registration of FIR against the driver of offending car.
12. The petitioner also furnished spot mahazar and spot sketch, which are marked as Ex.P.3.
The said document discloses that the police visited the place of incident after registration of FIR and the place of incident is described in the said documents.
In the mahazar also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
Ex.P.4 is Vehicle seizure mahazar.
The said document discloses the aspect of seizure of vehicle by the police.
As per the recitals of said document, the vehicle has been seized on the ground of its involvement in the cause of accident.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the seizure procedure conducted by the police.
The respondent No.1, being the owner of offending vehicle, does not appear to have questioned the seizure of the vehicle by the police.
The said document discloses the aspect of involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
13. Ex.P.6 is the Wound certificate which discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by petitioner in the road traffic accident.
Ex.P.5 is the IMV Reports, wherein the damages caused to both the vehicles are mentioned.
The vehicle will be inspected by the concerned after seizure of the same by the police.
The IMV report discloses the aspect damages being caused to the offending vehicle.
If the vehicle has not been involved in the accident, then the vehicle could not have been damaged, as mentioned in the IMV report.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle not provided any satisfactory explanation regarding the manner in which the vehicle got damaged.
The said document discloses the aspect of involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.

The I.O., after completion of investigation, filed the final report against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279, 338, 304(A) of IPC and U/s.134(a&b), 187 of M.V.Act as per Ex.P.8.
In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The police filed the final report after detailed investigation.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the correctness of the investigation.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondents to show that the investigation is not conducted in proper manner.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police.

In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondents and in the cross examination also, nothing to disprove or disbelieve the contention of petitioners could be elicited.

No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioners pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the Manish R vs Maheshwar Reddy Y on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64515664/
4 cause of accident.

sentences.text: 14. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
The respondents contended that the rider of motorcycle was also negligent and same has resulted in accident.
But, the respondents have not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to substantiate the said contention.
The materials on record do not disclose the aspect of negligence on the part of rider of motorcycle in the cause of accident.
The negligence on the part of rider of motorcycle is not forthcoming from the materials placed on record.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondents not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
On perusal of record, it discloses that accident was caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.8, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Regn.No.AP-04-TX-9855 by its driver and same has resulted in grievous injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
15. Issue No.2:
The petitioner succeeded in establishing that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle.
As Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

The Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc., in order to assess the compensation to which the petitioner is entitled.
i) Towards injury, pain and suffering:- The petitioner contended that due to accident he sustained injuries and underwent surgery and later discharged with an advice to take follow up treatment.
In order to prove the injuries sustained in the accident, the petitioner produced Wound certificate issued by Sridevi Institute of Medical Sciences & Research Hospital marked at Ex.P.6.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The said document discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by petitioner and that the injuries are grievous in nature.

The petitioner also furnished Ex.P.7 - Discharge Summary issued by Hosmat Hospital,
which discloses the aspect of availing treatment by petitioner for the injuries sustained by him in the accident.
Further, the petitioner examined Dr.Nagaraj.B.N as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P15 & 16 documents.
PW.2/doctor deposed that he examined the petitioner for assessment of permanent physical disability and assessed the disability to the right lower limb at 63% and to the whole body at 21%.
On consideration of the materials placed before the Tribunal, compensation of .50,000/- appears just and reasonable towards Pain and Suffering.
(ii) Towards Medical Expenses:- The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.

5
The petitioner contended that he took treatment at Hospital.
The petitioner has produced Medical bills amounting to .6,39,256/- marked at Ex.P.9 and medical prescriptions marked at Ex.P.13.
The respondent not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or disprove the said document.

PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondent and in the cross examination also,
nothing to rebut or doubt the medical bills, is elicited.
The respondents not rebutted the medical bills by placing cogent evidence.
The respondents not furnished satisfactory materials in order to rebut or controvert the medical bills furnished by petitioner.
So, this tribunal is of the view that compensation of .6,39,256/- appears just and reasonable towards medical expenses.
(iii) Towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant charges:- On perusal of records, the accident occurred on 15.03.2024 and the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient at the hospital.
On perusal of materials on record, the petitioner appears to have admitted as an inpatient at Hospital pertaining to the injuries sustained by him and availed treatment as an inpatient.

So,
during the time of treatment the petitioner might have required good food and extra nourishment.
PW.2/Doctor has produced Ex.P.7 - Discharge Summary, which discloses the aspect of availing treatment by petitioner as an inpatient from 16.03.2024 to 18.03.2024 i.e., for a period of 03 days.

Considering the said facts, the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of .500/- per day for 03 days to a sum of .1,500/- appears just and reasonable towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant.

(iv) Towards Conveyance:-
The petitioner is the resident of Panchamukhi Badavane, Antharasanahalli by Pass road, near KEB Northern Extension, Tumkur Town & District and he has admitted to hospital for treatment.
In order to prove this aspect the petitioner has produced discharge summary marked at Ex.P.7.
The petitioner might have incurred expenses for conveyance during the period of treatment.

Considering the injuries sustained and facts of the case, the tribunal is of view that the compensation of .10,000/-
appears just and proper towards conveyance charges.

(v) Towards loss of income during treatment:-
The petitioner contended that he was studying final year Diploma at Akshaya Polytechnic College, Tumakuru and was also earning a sum of .30,000/- per month was running a stationary shop at Tumkuru.
The petitioner has not furnished any satisfactory materials to show that he was earning .30,000/- per month.
No satisfactory materials are placed before the Tribunal to show the occupation and income of petitioner.
The petitioner not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to substantiate his contention regarding occupation and income.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, notional is to be taken into consideration.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as .16,500/-.
On perusal of record, it appears that petitioner might have not attended his work for some time due to accidental injuries.

Accordingly, the Manish R vs Maheshwar Reddy Y on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64515664/
6 petitioner is entitled for .20,000/- towards loss of income during treatment.

(vi) Towards Loss of future earning capacity:-
The petitioner has contended that due to accident, he was admitted as an inpatient at Hospital and sustained permanent disablement.
The petitioner also examined Dr.Nagaraj.B.N., who was working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Center, Bengaluru as PW.2.

sentences.text: PW.2/Doctor examined the patient clinically and radiologically to assess disabilities.

The doctor deposed that petitioner has sustained right proximal femur fracture with distal femur comminuted fracture, right leg both bones fracture, right hip acetabular fracture with posterior dislocation and underwent right hip open reduction and of the femoral head with posterior wall ORIF with RECON plate on 18.03.2024, CRIF with IMIL nail for the right tibia on 16.03.2024 and CRIF with right proximal femur & ORIF with LCP for the right distal femur on 19.03.2024 and was discharged.

Further PW.2 deposed that petitioner come with complains of pain in the right hip, unable to walk fast, unable to sit down,
squat and sit cross leg and lift heavy objects, Further on examination, the petitioner has mild limping gait, wasting of the right gluteal muscles, restricted right hip and knee movements.
Further as per X-ray of the right hip, right femur & right leg shows united fracture with implant in situ.
The doctor has assessed the disability to right lower limb at 63% and to the whole body at 21%.

In order to prove the disability, the doctor has produced clinical notes and X-rays marked at Ex.P.15 & 16.
PW.2 not stated that the petitioner could not be able to do his routine activities in a normal way.
The fractures are stated to have been united.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the petitioner to show that the petitioner is unable to do any work at all.
The injuries sustained by petitioner do not appear to cause much problem in doing his activities.
By considering the oral and documentary evidence and facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the petitioner can do his work with difficulty.
As per ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another and considering facts and circumstances of the case, the functional disability is assessed at 10%.

The accident occurred on 15.03.2024.

No satisfactory materials are placed before the Tribunal in order to disprove the contention of petitioner related to his age.

In the absence of materials to the contrary,
the document furnished by petitioner is to be considered for ascertaining the age.
As per the document, the age of petitioner was 19 years at the time of accident and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier.
As per Smt.Sarla Verma case multiplier applicable is '18'.
As per ratio laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay Kumar and another, this tribunal not deducted personal expenses of petitioner out of his gross income.

sentences.text: 18. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondents.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Regn.No.AP-04-TX-9855 by its driver.
So, the respondents being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.

19. Issue No.3:- In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for  compensation amount of .11,17,156/-
(Rupees Eleven Lakhs Seventeen Thousand One Hundred and Fifty Six only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
 Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and  severally liable to pay compensation to  petitioner.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

In the event of deposit of the said compensation amount, 40% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in any nationalized bank or scheduled bank and the remaining 60% shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper identification.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
If the vehicle has not been involved in the accident, then the vehicle could not have been damaged, as mentioned in the IMV report.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle not provided any satisfactory explanation regarding the manner in which the vehicle got damaged.
The said document discloses the aspect of involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The I.O., after completion of investigation, filed the final report against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279, 338, 304(A) of IPC and U/s.134(a&b), 187 of M.V.Act as per Ex.P.8.
In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The police filed the final report after detailed investigation.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the correctness of the investigation.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondents to show that the investigation is not conducted in proper manner.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police.
In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioners pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the Manish R vs Maheshwar Reddy Y on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64515664/
4 cause of accident.
The materials on record do not disclose the aspect of negligence on the part of rider of motorcycle in the cause of accident.
The negligence on the part of rider of motorcycle is not forthcoming from the materials placed on record.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondents not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
On perusal of record, it discloses that accident was caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
So, this tribunal is of the view that compensation of .6,39,256/- appears just and reasonable towards medical expenses.
The injuries sustained by petitioner do not appear to cause much problem in doing his activities.
By considering the oral and documentary evidence and facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the petitioner can do his work with difficulty.
As per ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another and considering facts and circumstances of the case, the functional disability is assessed at 10%.
The accident occurred on 15.03.2024.
As per the document furnished by petitioner, his age appears to be 19 years at the time of accident.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut the document furnished by petitioner related to his age.
No satisfactory materials are placed before the Tribunal in order to disprove the contention of petitioner related to his age.
In the absence of materials to the contrary,
the document furnished by petitioner is to be considered for ascertaining the age.
As per the document, the age of petitioner was 19 years at the time of accident and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier.

19. Issue No.3:- In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for  compensation amount of .11,17,156/-
(Rupees Eleven Lakhs Seventeen Thousand One Hundred and Fifty Six only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
 Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and  severally liable to pay compensation to  petitioner.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
In the event of deposit of the said compensation amount, 40% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in any nationalized bank or scheduled bank and the remaining 60% shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper identification.
After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA.No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.
The petitioner hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission from the Tribunal.
Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner on proper verification and identification or credit said amount to his account after expiry of three years period of deposit,
without waiting for further order of court.
The Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
